The city commission further adopts by reference the publication entitled "Retention Schedules for Local Government Records," printed by the Georgia Department of Archives and History as to both common and specific records, approved in April, 2000, and April, 2001, respectively, and as may be amended, altered, or modified from time to time, and to the extent compatible with the types of records generated and maintained by the city.
(Ord. No. 13-2001, § 1, 7-2-01)
198:
For purposes of this article, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivations, shall have the meaning given herein except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Agency means any city office, authority, department, division, board, commission, or other separate unit of city government created or established by federal, state, or local law, or under the jurisdiction of the Cedartown City Commission. Records of the Cedartown Municipal Court and the city attorney's office are expressly excluded from this article.
City means the City of Cedartown, a Municipal Corporation of the State of Georgia.
Records means all documents, papers, letters, maps, books, (except books in organized libraries), microfilm, magnetic tape, audio and video tapes, or any other material, regardless of physical form or characteristics, made or received pursuant to law or ordinance, in the performance of functions of any agency, or created in the normal course of business of any agency.
Record series means documents or records having similar physical characteristics or relating to a similar function or activity of the city and filed in a unified or uniform fashion.
Retention schedule means a set of instructions prescribing how long, where, and what form a record or record series shall be kept before disposition.
(Ord. No. 13-2001, § 1, 7-2-01)
201:
(a) Any city agency that wishes to retain a record or record series in a time, place, or manner different than that specified in the approved retention schedule for that agency shall submit a written petition to the records management officer for consideration. The petition shall include, but is not limited to, the type of record or record series and the reason or reasons for the desired action modifying the record retention schedule. These reasons shall be based on the legal, physical, administrative, and historical retention requirements and standards established by the records management officer and the city commission.
(b) The records management officer shall review each petition submitted by any city agency requesting a change in that agency's retention schedule and consider any and all evidence presented by the agency in its petition. The records management officer shall make a decision based upon the material submitted by the requesting agency to determine whether any modification of the existing retention schedule is warranted. Such decision shall be presented to the agency in writing within 20 days after the written request for a variation is submitted. If the state records committee has not issued final approval of any modifications adopted under this Code section, and a record or record series is scheduled for destruction pursuant to the existing retention schedule, the record or record series shall not be destroyed until notification and/or approval of any modifications to the retention schedule is received from the state records committee or its designee.
(c) Any city agency dissatisfied with the decision of the records management officer shall have ten days within which to appeal that decision to the city commission. After receiving the notice of appeal, the records management officer shall place the matter on the agenda of the next regular meeting of the city commission for consideration, and the commission's decision at that meeting shall be final. If under appeal, no record or record series scheduled for destruction pursuant to an existing retention schedule and listed in the petition of any agency under this Code section shall be destroyed until a final decision has been made by the city commission.
(d) Any decisions by either the records management officer or the city commission modifying, altering, or otherwise amending the existing record retention schedule shall be adopted in resolution form by the city commission and forwarded to the state records committee for approval.
(Ord. No. 13-2001, § 1, 7-2-01)
202:

(b) An archival depository will be selected to store those records that are determined to have permanent historical value.

(Ord. No. 13-2001, § 1, 7-2-01)

All procurements shall be carried out in compliance with one of the following four methods of procurement described below.
(1) Small purchase procedures. Small purchase procedures are relatively simple and informal procurement methods that are sound and appropriate for the procurement of relatively small quantities of equipment, materials, supplies or other property. In accordance with the requirements of the competitive bid law, small purchase procedures may be utilized for such purchases costing in the aggregate less than $25,000.00.
In accordance with the public works bid law, public works construction contracts of less than $250,000.00 may be let through the use of small purchase procedures without the need for sealed bids.
Small purchase procedures may also be utilized for the procurement of professional services.
When utilizing small purchase procedures, price or rate quotations must be obtained from an adequate number of qualified sources and, wherever possible, no less than three. Appropriate documentation of all small purchase procedures shall be maintained as required.
The lowest responsible proposer shall be selected, except in cases when documented exceptions may be granted with the approval of the city manager or chief financial officer.
Purchases less than the competitive bid law limit ($25,000.00), will be made in compliance with small purchase procedures. Competitive sealed bids may be used for smaller procurements if determined to be in the best interest of the city. Exceptions to this requirement may be granted by the city manager, for those purchases excluded from the competitive bid law requirements, when one of the following circumstances can be properly documented to substantiate the decision:
a. Items where the purchase price has been set by the federal government, the State of Georgia (e.g., state bid list), or a cooperative purchasing program (e.g. Sourcewell);
b. Requirements to maintain a degree of continuity with the original or existing decor, equipment, or programs, where an attempt to quote could result in operational or functional inconsistency;
c. When a quote attempt results in no response, orders will be placed with the first reliable source with suitable price, quality and delivery;
d. When lowest or best price has been previously determined by historical purchases; or
e. When the purchasing officer determines that three quotes cannot feasibly be obtained.
(2) Competitive sealed bids. In accordance with the requirements of the competitive bid law, competitive sealed bids shall be taken on contracts for all labor, services, or work, or for the purchase or lease of materials, equipment, supplies, or other personal property involving $25,000.00 or more. Procurements of professional services are exempt from the competitive bid law.
In accordance with the requirements of the public works law, competitive sealed bids must be utilized for public works construction projects totaling $250,000.00 or more. Sealed bids shall be publicly solicited through formal advertising. To be feasible to use competitive sealed bids, the following conditions must be present:
a. A complete, adequate and realistic specification or description of the purchase is available;
b. Two or more responsible vendors are willing and able to effectively compete for the business; and
c. The procurement lends itself to a firm fixed-price contract that allows selection of the successful bidder based principally on price. Cost plus a percentage of the cost is not allowed.
Procurements utilizing competitive sealed bids shall comply with the following:
a. Sufficient time must be allowed between bid solicitation and the date set for opening of bids.
b. Bids must be solicited from an adequate number of known suppliers. The invitation for bids must be publicly advertised (i.e., published at least once in The Polk County Standard Journal) or in accordance with applicable state law.
c. The invitation for bids, including specifications and pertinent attachments, must clearly define the items or services needed to allow the bidders to properly respond.
d. All bids must be opened publicly at the time and place stated in the invitation for bids.
e. A firm fixed-price contract award shall be made by written notice to the lowest responsible bidder whose bid conforms to the invitation for bids. If specified in the bidding documents, factors such as discounts, transportation costs and life cycle costs must be considered in determining which bid is lowest. Payment discounts may only be used to determine low bid when prior experience indicates that such discounts are generally taken.
f. Any or all bids may be rejected when there are sound documented business reasons in the best interest of the city.
(3) Competitive negotiation. Competitive negotiation may be used if conditions are not appropriate for the use of sealed bids. Either a fixed-price or a cost-reimbursable type contract may be awarded, as appropriate. If competitive negotiation procedures are utilized, the following requirements apply:
a. Proposals shall be solicited from an adequate number of qualified sources to permit reasonable competition. The request for proposals must be publicized and reasonable requests by other sources to compete must be honored to the maximum extent practicable.
b. The request for proposals shall identify all significant evaluation factors and their relative importance.
c. Mechanisms for technical evaluation of the proposals received, determinations of responsible vendors for the purpose of written or oral discussions and selection criteria for contract award, shall be provided.
d. Award may be made to the responsible offerer whose proposal will be most advantageous to the city, all factors considered. Unsuccessful offerers should be notified promptly.
Competitive negotiation procedures may be used for procurement of professional services. When utilizing competitive negotiation procedures for procurement of professional services, competitor's qualifications shall be evaluated and selection shall be subject to negotiation of fair and reasonable compensation for qualified competitors.
(4) Noncompetitive negotiation. Noncompetitive negotiation or "sole source" procurement is limited to the following situations:
a. The item or service is available from only one source.
b. Urgent public need or emergency will not allow for a delay caused by advertising.
c. After solicitation of a number of sources, competition is determined inadequate or only one response is received.
Contracts awarded utilizing noncompetitive negotiation procedures shall be made with responsible contractors or venders who are able to perform successfully under the terms and conditions of a proposed procurement document. Consideration shall be given to contractor integrity, record of past performance, financial and other technical resources or accessibility to other necessary resources.
When using the noncompetitive negotiation method of procurement, ensure that:
a. Proper documentation that one or more of the above circumstances existed;
b. There is no conflict of interest by the parties involved; and
c. Costs for the service(s) are clearly in line with applicable local, regional and/or state approved ranges or other acceptable industry standards.

Grant Program Compliance Supplement
Purpose.
To set forth the purchasing and financial management policies, authorities and procedures for the city, in relation to the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program, and any other grant programs implemented by the city, to assure compliance with applicable State of [Georgia] and federal laws and regulations. These policies and procedures are intended to coincide with and to supplement the city's standard operating procedures for procurement and financial management.
The policies and procedures outlined herein should be applied to all grant programs implemented by the city as applicable to help assure compliance with applicable federal regulations and guidelines.
Section 1. Authorization.
The city manager and/or chief financial officer are authorized to oversee all procurement activities, including all purchases and contracts, and shall be responsible for maintaining all financial records, documentation and files for the city's CDBG and other grant project(s).
Section 2. Coordination with the grant program administrator.
The city manager and/or chief financial officer are directed to undertake and initiate all grant procurement and financial management activities in cooperation and coordination with the grant program administrator, if any, selected by the city for each grant program.
The city manager and/or chief financial officer will assist the grant program administrator, as appropriate, in the financial and contractual administration of the program to ensure that payments for goods and/or services are issued only when:
A. The expense is an eligible grant program item and is appropriately budgeted in the approved grant program budget.
B. Sufficient and detailed source documentation is available.
C. The invoice has been approved for payment as required.
D. Contractors, subcontractors and vendors have performed in accordance with the terms and conditions of the approved contract or agreement.
Section 3. Role of the grant program administrator.
The city manager shall obtain advice and assistance regarding all procurements and the establishment and maintenance of all procurement and financial files and documentation from the program administrator, if any, for each grant project. The program administrator shall insure that all procurement and financial activities are carried out in compliance with applicable rules, regulations and procedures. The program administrator shall also insure that all expenses incurred are eligible items, are budgeted in the approved grant budget and are allocated to the appropriate budget items.
Section 4. Compliance with CDBG program requirements.
It is intended that all purchases and financial management activities related to CDBG program monies be carried out in compliance with all applicable rules, regulations and procedures as administered by the department of community affairs (DCA) as it presently exists and as it may be amended.
Any changes, modifications and/or updates to state and or federal laws, rules, regulations or procedures, which may cause conflict with these policies and procedures, will override that stated herein to the extent that the most stringent requirement will apply.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or have in his possession an open container of any alcoholic beverage:
(1) On any public street, sidewalk, park or other public place within the city, or upon or within any motor vehicle on the streets, sidewalks, parks and public places of the city unless said person is at or on the premises of an establishment with a license issued pursuant to this article; or
(2) While on private property, open to public view, without the express permission of the owner, agent or person in lawful possession thereof.
(Ord. No. 3-2003, § 3, 8-11-03)
247:
(a) No holder of any alcoholic beverage license or his agents, employees, or representatives shall knowingly furnish, sell, or offer for sale any alcoholic beverages to a person under 21 years of age. "SALE OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES TO MINORS STRICTLY PROHIBITED."

(e) The municipal court, in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 36-32-10, is granted jurisdiction to try and dispose of a first offense violation of O.C.G.A. § 3-3-23, relating to furnishing alcoholic beverages to, and purchase and possession of alcoholic beverages by, a person under 21 years of age, if the offense occurred within the corporate limits of the city. 254:
License fees shall be such as are specified from time to time by ordinance adopted by the city commission. License fees shall be payable in advance for the entire year as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges, beginning on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year. 255: No license shall be issued under this article unless the applicant therefor has fully paid all license fees and taxes, other applicable business taxes and ad valorem taxes due to the city for the business location.
258:
No alcoholic beverage license shall be granted to any applicant, unless that applicant meets the following standards of qualifications for the granting of a license. If such qualifications are not met, this shall be considered as grounds for denial of a license, in addition to the provisions for the granting of the license as set forth in section 6-64:
(1) All applicants for a retail license must show financial responsibility. The city commission may require all applicants to provide financial statements and other evidence of financial responsibility in conjunction with any application. All applicants for a license must be of good character, and all operators, managers, clerks and other employees that may be involved in the sale of malt beverages shall be of like character. Corporate or firm applicants shall be of good business reputation.
(2) The applicant must be a citizen of the United States or a resident alien, and a resident of the county for a period of one year preceding the date of filing the application, except as provided in subsection (6) of this section. No license shall be granted to an applicant who has been convicted under federal, state or local law for a criminal offense involving alcoholic beverages, gambling, crimes involving moral turpitude or tax law violations, or any other conviction, if such conviction tends to indicate that the applicant would not maintain the operation for which a license is being sought in conformity with federal, state or local laws of the city.
(3) The applicant shall not have had revoked, for cause, such as violation of regulations, or improper operations, within five years next preceding his application, any license issued to him by any city or county in the state, this state, or any other state, to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind.
(4) The applicant shall be either the owner of the premises for which the license is held or the owner of a lease thereon.
(5) The applicant shall be active in, and solely responsible for the management and operation of, the business for which the license is granted.
(6) If the applicant is a partnership or corporation, then either a partner, outlet manager or corporate agent must conduct the business on the licensed premises, but such person does not have to reside within the county.
(7) Any misstatement or concealment of fact in the application shall be grounds for denial of consideration of the application or revocation of any license if this is discovered after the license is granted. The applicant shall be subject to prosecution for perjury under the laws of the state for such conduct.
(8) The city commission, in its discretion, may consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, application or the proposed location of the business; including, but not limited to, any report which may be obtained from the chief of police, or his designee, and the other standards for review of license applications as set forth in section 6-64. If, in the judgment of the city commission, circumstances are such that the granting of the license would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.
(9) If the application is otherwise approved after consideration as provided in this Code, the applicant must obtain a federal beer stamp and a state retail beer license before beginning operation.
(Code 1969, § 3-20; Ord. No. 17-2000, § 1, 12-11-00)
259: The application form for an alcoholic beverage license shall be obtained from the city clerk and filed with the city clerk. It shall be subscribed by the applicant under oath, and shall be fully and completely executed. If the applicant is a partnership, all partners shall execute the same, and if the applicant is a corporation, it shall be executed by the president and secretary of the corporation. There shall also be attached to the application a bank money order, certified check or like remittance for the license fee in full. When the verified application, with the affidavit of publication and payment of the license fee, is filed with the city clerk, it shall be transmitted to the city commission for review. The application shall be reviewed under the retail license qualifications and standards for review contained in this Code, together with any and all other applicable federal, state or local laws which may govern the issuance of this alcoholic beverage license.
260:
An application for an alcoholic beverage license shall be completely and fully executed, and each question on the form provided shall be answered accurately. Failure of an applicant to furnish accurately all data, information and records required by the application form as well as failure to accompany the application with the payment of the prescribed fee as approved by the City of Cedartown Commission in the schedule of fees and charges shall be deemed just cause for denying the application with prejudice.
(Ord. No. 7-2019, § 2(Exh. A), 12-9-19)
261:
(a) After the application has been completed and submitted to the city commission for a decision, in making a determination, the commission shall be guided by the following factors:
(1) The report of the chief of police concerning the investigation into the application.
(2) The criminal record of the applicant and outlet manager, if applicable, and the general good character, reputation and financial responsibility of the applicant, provided that nonpayment of federal, state, county or city taxes shall be prima facie evidence of lack of financial responsibility.
(3) Whether all of the information or statements contained in the application are complete.
(4) Evidence presented to the commission for or against the application, at the time and place set for an initial decision on the application by the commission.
(5) Whether any license for the sale of alcoholic beverages previously issued for such location has been revoked for cause by the city commission.
(6) Whether the applicant holds or possesses any other license for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine issued by the city.
(7) The history or reputation of the building or establishment proposed for the outlet for prostitution or other sex offenses; fighting, shooting, stabbing or other violence; gambling, illegal dealing in alcoholic beverages or drugs; or other similar violations of the laws of this state or the United States of America.
(8) Whether the applicant meets all of the retail license qualifications set forth in section 6-61.
(9) Whether the license is for a location which comes within the provisions of prohibited locations, as such term is defined in section 6-131.
(10) Whether the proposed location has adequate off-the-street parking facilities or other parking available for its patrons, and whether the location would tend to increase and promote traffic congestion and resulting hazards therefrom.
(11) The nature of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location; that is, whether the same is predominately residential, industrial or business.
(b) A decision on a license application shall be made at the next regular or special meeting of the city commission under the provisions of this article. Licenses, if granted, shall be issued by the city clerk upon payment of the license fee. All decisions of the commission shall be in accordance with section 6-66.
(Code 1969, § 3-22; Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
262: Whenever there shall be a change in any of the facts reported to the city commission in the application for a license after such license has been granted, it shall be the duty of the licensee, within ten business days after such change, to report the same to the city clerk in writing.

(a) In addition to the provisions of this article, licensees are also charged with the responsibility for adhering to any other provisions of this Code, as well as the statutes and laws of the state and of the United States relating to the operation of their businesses.

267:
If the city commission revokes, suspends or fails to renew any license which has been issued by the commission under this article, the city commission may, notwithstanding the other provisions herein, review such revocation, suspension or failure to renew and may reinstate such license, subject to all of the following conditions:
(1) Such review cannot be held until at least one year after the date of the revocation, suspension or failure to renew.
(2) The original licensee against whom the revocation, suspension or failure to renew action was taken must make application in writing for reinstatement of his license after the lapse of the one-year period.
(3) The original licensee must have remained in the same business, except for the selling of alcoholic beverages, at the same location continuously since such revocation, suspension or failure to renew.
(4) The original licensee must, at the time of the review, be qualified in all respects for the same type license originally issued to him, except for those provisions in section 6-61 concerning violations relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages, if the revocations, suspension or failure to renew was a result of such violation.

268:
(a) The following shall be considered just cause for the suspension or revocation of a license issued under this article:
(1) The performance of any act prohibited by this chapter or the failure to perform any act required by this chapter as well as the violation of any law, state or federal, relating to the business of the licensee. (2) The entry of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere, or the conviction of any licensee, partner, or any officer, director or stockholder of a licensee corporation with respect to a charge of violation of any of the laws of the United States or of the state relating to alcohol control, or any crime, whether a felony or not, involving moral turpitude.
(3) Any other act or omission with respect to the operation of a business licensed hereunder which the city commission shall find to be contrary to the public interest, or which shall render the licensee or the business location unfit for the continued operation of the business.
(b) In addition to the matters enumerated in subsection (a) of this section, the following shall be considered just cause for suspension or revocation of a license for retail sales of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises: The occurrence on two or more occasions within any 12-month period of fights, disorderly conduct, drunkenness, breach of the peace, and other similar conduct whether the same be committed by the licensee or by customers or others.
(Ord. No. 1-2003, § 2, 3-10-03)
269:
(a) Prior to taking any potentially adverse action with regard to a license issued under this chapter or Code, the city commission shall afford the licensee notice of a hearing and an opportunity to be heard. The licensee shall be given at least five days' personal written notice of the hearing which may be held at a duly called regular or special meeting of the commission.
(b) At the time and place appointed for a hearing, the licensee may be represented by counsel. The license holder shall have the opportunity to present testimony, documentary evidence, or any other relevant evidence it may have, and cross-examine opposing witnesses.
(c) after the hearing, and after considering all evidence properly presented to it, the city commission shall take action with regard to the city alcoholic beverage license as may be warranted by the evidence, in its sole judgment and discretion. 272: When a license has been revoked under the provisions of this article, no application for a new alcoholic beverage license for the same location will be received for a period of 12 months and no application for a new license from the licensee involved shall be received for a period of 24 months.

(1) Sell malt beverages and/or wine to a minor.
(2) Sell malt beverages and/or wine to any person who is intoxicated or already under the influence of any alcoholic beverages.
(3) Sell or permit to be consumed malt beverages and/or wine on the licensed premises on any day or at any time when such sale or consumption is prohibited by law.
(4) Permit any disorderly conduct or breach of the peace in or on the licensed premises.
(5) Possess, sell or offer for sale any liquor, spirits, or other alcoholic beverages, if the sale or possession of such beverages is not authorized under the license granted to the holder.
